## Roe (`type: roe`) {#sec-ch04-roe}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- A linearised solver: the centred flux minus a characteristic decomposition of the jump.
- Switch: `type: roe`, and it is the YAML default when no type is named.
- Roe averages use the square-root density weighting; species rows ride on the entropy wave.
- Writes a face pressure.
- No entropy fix: the wave speeds are used as absolute values with a floor, not corrected at a sonic point.
:::

Roe's solver linearises the problem about an average state chosen so that the linearised jump reproduces the
exact flux difference. The flux is then the average of the two physical fluxes minus the sum over waves of
their strength times their speed, which is where the upwinding comes from.

### Derivation

The averaging is the square-root weighting, at `sqrtdl` ([`roe_impl.h:39-48`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/roe_impl.h#L39-L48)): each quantity is weighted by
the square root of its density so that the linearised system reproduces the jump exactly. The sound speed
follows from the averaged enthalpy and velocity at `cs_sq` ([`roe_impl.h:117-118`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/roe_impl.h#L117-L118)), with a floor applied
through `roe_max` so that a non-positive argument cannot reach the square root.

The three wave strengths at `alpha_m` ([`roe_impl.h:137-140`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/roe_impl.h#L137-L140)) are the familiar ones: two acoustic strengths
carrying the velocity jump against the pressure jump over the squared sound speed, and the two tangential
momentum strengths riding on the entropy wave.

The species rows are the part specific to snapy. Each gets its own entropy-wave strength at
`alpha_n` ([`roe_impl.h:155-161`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/roe_impl.h#L155-L161)), built as the jump in that species' partial density minus the pressure
jump times the species' share. That construction is what keeps a species from being generated at a contact,
and no source in the repository derives it; it is recorded here from the code.

### Numerical method

The body is [`roe_impl.h:24-217`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/roe_impl.h#L24-L217). It assembles the centred flux, then subtracts half the sum of
each wave's absolute speed times its strength times its right eigenvector, with the mass and species rows at
`alpha_n` ([`roe_impl.h:149-161`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/roe_impl.h#L149-L161)).

The absolute speeds at `spd_0` ([`roe_impl.h:127-129`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/roe_impl.h#L127-L129)) are taken directly, with no entropy fix. At a sonic
point one of the three speeds passes through zero and its dissipation vanishes with it, which is the classical
condition under which a Roe solver can admit an expansion shock. Nothing in the code detects that case.

The face pressure is written at `face_pressure` ([`roe_impl.h:119-124`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/roe_impl.h#L119-L124)).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- No entropy fix. At a sonic point the dissipation of the vanishing wave vanishes with it, and a Roe solver in
  that state can admit an expansion shock. No test in the repository exercises a transonic rarefaction.
:::

1. **Default by omission.** This is the solver a deck gets when it names none, while every shipped example
   names LMARS. The two have different dissipation, so an unset key is a silent change of scheme.
2. **Floors in place of a fix.** The `roe_max` floors keep the square root defined but say nothing about the
   accuracy of the linearisation where they bind.
